args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release marked healthy in production. Post-rollback status: healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 was promoted to production. Follow-up: root-cause the v2.3.1 regression and review why an unhealthy RC was promoted.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Cause:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release marked healthy in production. All three regions now run it, and the error rate has dropped to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says what failed, what I did and what still needs doing. There were no open incidents before, so it isn't a duplicate.

**Still to do:** The version tested in staging before v2.3.1 (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy there, so v2.3.1 reached production after failing in staging. The incident lists two follow-ups: find what broke in v2.3.1, and find out why it was released despite failing in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
